# Terminals: grouped sidebar, tabs, 1/2/4-pane split with terminal or run panes, Ctrl Space prefix, restart and reconnect (GMD-08)

## What to build

Rebuild `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.tsx` as on boards `07-terminals-light-2-2-split`, `08-terminals-dark`, `09-terminals-800-px`, and the TERMINALS states on `19-empty-loading-error-dialogs-light` (empty; exited / reconnecting; the close dialog). Extend the terminal server with the foreground process name, restart and rename.

**Sidebar** (≈280px):

- **Header:** "Terminals <count>" and a primary **New** button.
- **Filter chips:**
  - "N working" (live)
  - "N idle" (warn)
  - "N other" (mute; exited)

  Each chip toggles a filter, synced with `?filter=`.
- **Sections:**
  - **NEEDS YOU**: every `idle` terminal.
  - **One per workspace:** caps label `OWNER/REPO`, the fullPath upper-cased, with a count. It holds that workspace's terminals that aren't idle.
  - **WORKSPACES ROOT:** terminals without a workspace.
- **Items** (52px tall):
  - A tone glyph and the title.
  - A sub-line in mono `--fg3`: `<process> · working 14s` / `<workspace short name> · idle 4m` / `exited 0 · 22m ago`.
    - The process is `TerminalInfo.process`.
    - "working Ns" counts from the start of the current output burst. Use `lastOutputAt` and createdAt if nothing better is available.
    - "idle Nm" counts since `lastOutputAt`.
  - At the right:
    - A small mono chip with the last 4 chars of each live run in the terminal's workspace (from `useOverview().runs` with `live` and matching `workspaceId`). Clicking it opens that run in a pane.
    - The pane number badge (1–4) when the terminal is shown in a pane. The focused pane's badge is filled with the accent colour.
- **Keyboard:** j/k/Enter move through the items and open them.
- **Footer hints:** `Ctrl Space a` next idle, `Ctrl Space 1–4` focus pane.

**Tab bar:** one tab per open item, terminal or run.

- A terminal tab has a tone dot, its title and ×. A run tab is labelled `run <last4>`.
- Clicking a tab puts it in the focused pane.
- At the right, layout buttons: 1 pane, 2 side by side, 2×2. The active one is highlighted.
- Layout, open tabs and pane assignment are saved in `localStorage["gm.terminals.layout"]` and survive a reload. Drop ids that no longer exist.

**Panes** (grid, 8px gap):

- **Header:**
  - The pane number, the title (bold), the workspace fullPath (`--fg3`, ellipsis) and a status badge. A terminal shows `working`, or `idle 4m · waiting on you` in warn, or `exited N`.
  - For a terminal with a live run in its workspace, a chip `run 44c2 ↗` that opens the run in the next free pane, or in pane 2.
  - Maximise (toggles a temporary 1-pane view of this pane) and × (close).
- The focused pane has a 2px accent border.
- **Terminal pane:**
  - The xterm in a `--term` background, dark in both themes.
  - When the process has exited, a bottom bar on a `--bad`-tinted dark background: "Process exited with code N", **Restart** (POST `/api/terminals/:id/restart`, then reattach; the scrollback stays) and **Close**.
  - When the WebSocket drops unexpectedly (not code 4404, not on unmount), an amber bar: "Reconnecting to the container… your scrollback is kept on the server.". Reconnect with backoff (0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, max 5 s); on reconnect the server's `replay` resets and redraws the screen.
- **Run pane:**
  - Header: `run <last4>`, the workspace, the run status badge, and "open ↗" (to `/runs/<ws>/<id>`).
  - Body: the run's live iframe (`viewUrl`) while live, else `<TaskGraph graph={detail.graph} tasks={detail.tasks} compact />` (from `pages/TaskGraph.tsx`, already built by the run-detail task) with data from `GET /api/runs/:ws/:runId`, polled every 2 s.
- Only visible panes mount an xterm. Keep the existing `TerminalView` behaviour: replay on attach, FitAddon with ResizeObserver, focus on show.

**Closing:**

- × on a tab or pane, or `Ctrl Space x`, closes the terminal.
- A `working` terminal first opens `<ConfirmDialog title='Close “<title>”?' body="<process> is still working (output Ns ago). Closing the tab ends the process and its scrollback." cancelLabel="Keep running" confirmLabel="Close terminal" tone="danger">`.
- An idle or exited terminal closes right away (DELETE `/api/terminals/:id`).
- Closing a run tab just removes it.

**New terminal:** the **New** button and `Ctrl Space n` open a small popover/dialog:

- **Workspace** select: "Workspaces root" or a workspace. Defaults to the workspace of the focused pane.
- **Title**, optional.
- **Create**: POST `/api/terminals` `{workspaceId?, title?}`, then the new terminal goes into the focused pane.

`?workspace=<id>` still creates a terminal right away (keep today's behaviour, and keep it from creating two in StrictMode). `?focus=<id>` puts that terminal in the focused pane. `?run=<ws>/<runId>` opens that run in a pane.

**Empty state:** no terminals at all. A dark panel with "No terminals open", "A new terminal opens in the selected workspace, or in /workspaces if none is selected." and **New terminal** `<Kbd>Ctrl Space n</Kbd>`.

**Ctrl Space prefix:** press Ctrl+Space anywhere on the page, including inside an xterm. Use xterm's `attachCustomKeyEventHandler` to intercept Ctrl+Space and return false. Show a small "Ctrl Space…" hint chip for 1.5 s while waiting for the next key:

- `n`: new terminal
- `x`: close the focused pane's item
- `1`–`4`: focus that pane
- `|`: cycle the layout (1 → 2 → 4)
- `a`: focus the next idle terminal, putting it in the focused pane

The key after the prefix is NOT sent to the terminal.

**Under 900px:** the sidebar becomes a drawer (a toggle button in the tab bar), and the layout is forced to 1 pane (board 09).

**Server** (`apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts` and `routes/terminals.ts`):

- `TerminalInfo.process?: string`: node-pty's `proc.process`, the foreground process name, read in `info()` inside try/catch. Keep `title` separate.
- `TerminalManager.restart(id): TerminalInfo`: only for an exited terminal (409 otherwise).
  - Spawns a new pty with the same cwd, env, title, workspaceId and size.
  - Keeps the old scrollback and appends `\r\n` so new output starts on a fresh line.
  - Clears `exitCode` and re-wires `onData`/`onExit` to the existing listeners.
- `POST /api/terminals/:id/restart` → 200 `info`, 404 for an unknown id, 409 when it is running.
- `PATCH /api/terminals/:id` with `{title}` (1–200 chars) → 200 `info`. Double-clicking a tab title renames it inline.
- The WebSocket keeps working across a restart. A socket attached before the restart gets the new process's data. The simplest way: listeners stay in `term.listeners`; on exit, keep the listener registered (don't remove it). Today `attach()` only adds the listener while running. Change that, so an attachment to an exited terminal also stays registered and receives data after a restart. Send `{type:"restart"}` to attached sockets so the client clears the exit bar.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/Terminals.tsx` (169 lines) and `Terminals.test.tsx`: today's tabs, sidebar, `?workspace=` handling. Rewrite them.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/components/TerminalView.tsx` (82 lines): the xterm + WebSocket client (`replay`/`data`/`exit` messages, `resize`/`input` messages, close code 4404). Extend it with:
  - reconnect
  - a `{type:"restart"}` message
  - callbacks `onExit(code)` / `onConnection(state)`
  - a `--term` theme: xterm `theme: { background: <--term>, foreground: <--termfg> }`, reading the CSS variables with `getComputedStyle`
  - the Ctrl+Space handler hook
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.ts` (240 lines):
  - `Term`, `TerminalInfo`, `create()` (lines 109–153), `attach()` (164–189), `kill`/`remove`, `info()` (227–240)
  - `WORKING_MS = 3000` is the working/idle threshold.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` (79 lines): the routes and the WS handler.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/terminals.test.ts`, `routes/terminals.test.ts`: the test patterns (real ptys running `bash`/`sh`, real WebSocket clients via `ws`).
- `docs/design/graph-manager/07-terminals-light-2-2-split.png` / `.html` (exact sidebar, tabs, panes, chips), `08-…png` (dark), `09-terminals-800-px.png`, `19-…png` (empty, exited, reconnecting, close dialog).
- `docs/design/graph-manager/00-ia-proposal-react-notes.txt`: keyboard model and xterm notes.

## Step-by-step tasks

1. Server: `process`, `restart`, `PATCH` title, listener persistence and the `restart` message, with tests in `terminals.test.ts` and `routes/terminals.test.ts`:
   - restart after `exit 3` gives a new process
   - the replay keeps the old output
   - a socket attached before the restart receives new output
   - `process` is a non-empty string for a running shell
2. Client types: add `process?` to `TerminalInfo` in `src/web/types.ts`.
3. Rewrite `TerminalView.tsx`, `Terminals.tsx`, plus `pages/Terminals.css`, `pages/TerminalSidebar.tsx`, `pages/TerminalPane.tsx`, `pages/layout.ts` (pure layout state: open, assign, close, cycle, persist; unit-tested).
4. Tests (jsdom, mock `@xterm/xterm` like the existing `Terminals.test.tsx` does):
   - sidebar grouping (needs you / workspace / root)
   - filter chips
   - the layout buttons set 1, 2 or 4 panes
   - closing a working terminal asks, an idle one doesn't
   - the exited bar with Restart calls the endpoint
   - `layout.ts` persistence drops unknown ids
   - the prefix: Ctrl+Space then `n` opens the new-terminal dialog, and `1`–`4` focus panes

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In a real browser: open 4 terminals, pick 2×2, and each pane runs independently (`echo` in each).
- [ ] A fake run started in one terminal (`graph-execution diamond --spec spec.md --provider fake --web` in a cloned workspace holding the engine's diamond fixture) shows a run chip in that terminal's header and sidebar item, and the chip opens the run view in a pane.
- [ ] `exit 1` shows "Process exited with code 1". **Restart** gives a new prompt in the same folder, with the old output still above it.
- [ ] Restarting the graph-manager server while the page is open shows the reconnecting bar. On a server restart the terminals are gone, so the bar ends in "terminal not found". Within one server lifetime, killing only the socket (e.g. `agent-browser` offline/online, or closing the WS from devtools) reconnects with the scrollback.
- [ ] Ctrl+Space then `n`, `x`, `1`–`4`, `|` and `a` work while focus is inside an xterm, and the letter does not reach the shell.
- [ ] The sidebar shows `bash · …` (or the shell's name) and switches to `node` while graph-execution runs in the foreground.
- [ ] The layout survives a reload.
- [ ] Screenshots match boards 07, 08 and 09 (800px, sidebar as a drawer, one pane).
- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test -w graph-manager` pass.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test -w graph-manager -- erminal layout
npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager   # then agent-browser on /terminals
```

---

## Shared context (same in every task of this run)

**Hard rule: client changes only.** Never modify anything under `packages/graph-execution/` (the engine). Read it, import from `graph-execution/api`, and run its CLI, but all changes go in `apps/graph-manager/` and docs (`TESTING.md`, `docs/`).

**Repo.** npm-workspaces monorepo. The engine is `packages/graph-execution` (published CLI, library entry `graph-execution/api` = `packages/graph-execution/src/api.ts`). The product is `apps/graph-manager`: Fastify 5 server in `src/server/`, React 19 + react-router 7 + Vite UI in `src/web/`, tests with vitest (server: `fastify.inject` via `src/server/test-helpers.ts`; UI: `// @vitest-environment jsdom` + `@testing-library/react` with `fetch` stubbed by `vi.stubGlobal`, see `src/web/App.test.tsx`). The spec is `docs/prd/graph-manager-design.md`.

**The design.** `docs/design/graph-manager/` holds every board of the design as `NN-name.png` (screenshot, open it with your image-reading tool and LOOK at it), `NN-name.txt` (all its text) and `NN-name.html` (its real HTML/CSS, fonts stripped; copy measurements, colors and structure from here). Boards: `00-ia-proposal-react-notes`, `01-design-system`, `02-component-nav-rail`, `03-login-light`, `04-login-dark`, `05-runs-dashboard-light-start-run-open`, `06-runs-dashboard-dark`, `07-terminals-light-2-2-split`, `08-terminals-dark`, `09-terminals-800-px`, `10-run-detail-live-light`, `11-run-detail-live-dark`, `12-run-detail-finished-800-px`, `13-run-detail-landed-create-pr-light`, `14-run-detail-landed-create-pr-dark`, `15-workspaces-clone-light`, `16-workspaces-clone-dark`, `17-settings-forges-light`, `18-settings-forges-dark`, `19-empty-loading-error-dialogs-light`, `20-empty-loading-error-dialogs-dark`. Mock data in the boards (octo/hello, dev-vm-01, counts) is illustrative: show real data from the API. Where a board shows something impossible with real data, keep the layout and use real values.

**Shared UI contracts.** Tasks run in parallel, so everyone uses these exact names. Task 2 creates the `ui/` kit, task 3 creates the shell, overview and keys; later tasks only consume them (and may add optional fields to shared types in place).

- `apps/graph-manager/src/web/ui/tokens.css`: CSS variables `--bg --sf --sf2 --bd --bd2 --fg --fg2 --fg3 --ac --acbg --term --termfg` (values from `01-design-system`), status tones `--live --live-bg --ok --ok-bg --warn --warn-bg --bad --bad-bg --mute --mute-bg --rev --rev-bg`, `--space-1`…`--space-8` (4 8 12 16 20 24 32 48 px), `--radius-sm/md/lg` (4/6/10), `--control-h` 36px, `--control-h-dense` 32px, `--row-h` 40px, `--nav-w` 232px, `--rail-w` 56px, `--dur-fast` 120ms, `--dur-base` 180ms, `--font-sans` (Geist Variable, system-ui…), `--font-mono` (Geist Mono Variable, ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas). Light on `:root`, dark on `:root[data-theme="dark"]`. Components use only `var(--…)`, never hex.
- `ui/base.css` (imported once in `main.tsx`): global classes `.btn` (+ `.btn-primary`, `.btn-danger`, `.btn-ghost`, `.btn-sm`), `.input`, `.select`, `.textarea`, `.field` (`.field-label`, `.field-hint`, `.field-error`), `.card`, `.table` with `.table-row` / `.table-row.focused` / `.table-group`, `.chip`, `.mono`, `.num` (tabular-nums), `.muted`, `.page`, `.page-header`. Focus ring: 2px `var(--ac)` outline, 2px offset, on every focusable element.
- `ui/status.ts`: `type Tone = "live" | "ok" | "warn" | "bad" | "mute" | "rev"`, `type Glyph = "pulse" | "dot" | "ring" | "dashed" | "diamond" | "bar" | "half"`, `toneOf(kind: "run" | "task" | "term", value: string, exitCode?: number): Tone`, `glyphOf(kind, value, exitCode?): Glyph`. Mapping: run running→live/pulse, applied→ok/dot, done→mute/ring, aborted→mute/bar, failed→bad/diamond, review→rev/half; task running|validating|merging→live/pulse, merged→ok/dot, failed→bad/diamond, pending→mute/dashed; term working→live/pulse, idle→warn/half, exited with 0→mute/ring, exited with ≠0→bad/diamond.
- `ui/StatusBadge.tsx`: `<StatusBadge kind="run"|"task"|"term" value={string} exitCode?={number} label?={string} />` renders `<span className="badge tone-<tone>" data-tone=<tone>>` with the glyph and `label ?? value` (term exited shows `exited <code>`). Also exports `<StatusGlyph tone glyph />` and `<LiveDot />` (blue pulsing dot + "live").
- `ui/Icon.tsx`: `<Icon name=… size?={16} />`, inline SVG, `currentColor`. Names: `logo runs terminal folder settings search plus close external moon sun monitor logout chevron-left chevron-right chevron-down branch maximize layout-1 layout-2 layout-4 info git refresh`.
- `ui/Drawer.tsx`: `<Drawer open title onClose footer?>` right-side panel (360px; full width under 900px), Esc closes, focus goes back to the opener.
- `ui/Dialog.tsx`: `<ConfirmDialog open title body confirmLabel cancelLabel? tone?: "danger" | "primary" onConfirm onCancel extraAction?: {label, onClick} />` (role `dialog`, Esc = cancel, shows `Esc` kbd on Cancel).
- `ui/Segmented.tsx`: `<Segmented options={{value, label}[]} value onChange ariaLabel />` (role `radiogroup`, buttons role `radio`).
- `ui/Kbd.tsx` `<Kbd>Ctrl K</Kbd>`; `ui/ForgeChip.tsx` `<ForgeChip forge="github"|"gitlab" />` (mono caps chip GITHUB/GITLAB); `ui/Skeleton.tsx` `<SkeletonRows rows={4} />`; `ui/EmptyState.tsx` `<EmptyState title body? action? />`; `ui/Progress.tsx` `<Progress value={0..1} tone={Tone} />`.
- `ui/toast.tsx`: `<ToastProvider>` and `useToast(): { show(t: { tone: "ok" | "bad" | "live"; text: string; action?: { label: string; to?: string; onClick?: () => void } }): void }`. Bottom-right stack, auto-dismiss after 6 s.
- `ui/theme.ts`: `type ThemePref = "system" | "light" | "dark"`, `getThemePref()`, `setThemePref(p)` (`localStorage["gm.theme"]`, every access in try/catch), `applyTheme()` (sets `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` to the resolved `light`/`dark`, follows `matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")` while `system`), `useTheme(): { pref, setPref, resolved }`.
- `src/web/types.ts`: the client copies of the API shapes: `RunSummary`, `TerminalInfo`, `WorkspaceEntry`, `ForgesInfo`. Add optional fields in place when your task adds them on the server.
- `src/web/overview.tsx`: `<OverviewProvider>` and `useOverview(): { runs: RunSummary[]; terminals: TerminalInfo[]; workspaces: WorkspaceEntry[]; workspacesRoot?: string; forges: ForgesInfo; loaded: boolean; updatedAt?: number; failures: number; stale: boolean; refresh(): Promise<void> }`. It polls `GET /api/runs`, `/api/terminals`, `/api/workspaces`, `/api/forges` every 2 s with `Promise.allSettled`, pauses while `document.hidden`, keeps the last good data, and sets `stale` after 3 failed polls in a row. Also `<UpdatedAgo />` ("updated 1s ago", amber when stale) and `<StaleBanner />` ("Can't reach the server. Showing data from 14s ago. Retrying…").
- `src/web/keys.ts`: `useKey(combo, handler, opts?: { enabled?: boolean; allowInInput?: boolean })` with combos like `"s"`, `"p"`, `"/"`, `"Escape"`, `"Ctrl+k"`, `"Ctrl+Enter"`; `isTypingTarget(el)` (input, textarea, select, contenteditable, or inside `.xterm`); `useListNav(count, { onOpen(i) }): [index, setIndex]` (j/k/Enter, ignored while typing). The shell handles `g r|t|w|s`, `Ctrl+k`, and `/` (focuses the first `[data-filter]` element on the page).
- Routes and query strings: `/runs?status=failed|live|ready&workspace=<id>`, `/runs/:ws/:runId`, `/terminals?workspace=<id>` (opens a new terminal there), `?focus=<terminalId>`, `?filter=working|idle|other`, `?run=<ws>/<runId>` (opens that run in a pane), `/workspaces?clone=1` (opens the clone drawer), `/settings`. Page roots keep `data-testid="page-runs" | "page-terminals" | "page-workspaces" | "page-settings" | "page-run-detail" | "page-login"`.
- Each page keeps its CSS in its own file next to it (`pages/Runs.css` imported by `pages/Runs.tsx`), so parallel tasks don't edit one stylesheet.

**Look at what you build.** For any UI change, build and run graph-manager and look at it in a real browser with `agent-browser` (installed globally; run `agent-browser skills get core` once if you need its command reference):

```bash
npm run build -w graph-execution && npm run build -w graph-manager
GM_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
node apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-forge.mjs 7421 $GM_DIR/forge &      # fake GitHub/GitLab; tokens gh-good / gl-good
GM_PASSWORD=pw GM_PORT=7420 GM_DATA_DIR=$GM_DIR/data GM_WORKSPACES_DIR=$GM_DIR/ws \
  GM_GITHUB_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7421/github node apps/graph-manager/dist/server/main.js &
agent-browser open http://127.0.0.1:7420/ && agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser set viewport 1440 900 && agent-browser screenshot /tmp/gm.png   # then open /tmp/gm.png and compare it with the board
```

Use another port if 7420/7421 are taken. Log in with `pw`. Check light and dark (`agent-browser eval 'document.documentElement.dataset.theme'`). Start runs with `--provider fake` only, never a real provider. Stop the servers by PID (`kill <pid>`), never by name. More recipes are in the graph-manager section of `TESTING.md`.

**Validation.**

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-manager
git diff --stat -- packages/graph-execution     # must be empty: the engine is read-only for this run
```

Known environment failure: `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.test.ts` "exits 2 at startup when --provider claude is not on the PATH" fails wherever a real `claude` is installed next to `node`. Ignore that one case only.
